name: Grow herbs on a windowsill
blurb: Fresh herbs within arm’s reach of the hob. The trick nobody mentions is that supermarket pots are dozens of seedlings crammed together and are designed to die.
gear: Pots with drainage and decent compost
Seeds or young plants: basil, mint, parsley, chives, thyme
steps: Choose by your light: mint, chives and parsley cope with less sun; basil and thyme need the brightest spot you have.
If you buy a supermarket pot, split it into three or four smaller clumps and repot them — crowded roots are why they collapse in a fortnight.
Use pots with drainage and a free-draining compost; herbs hate sitting wet.
Harvest correctly: pinch basil above a leaf pair to make it bush out, and cut chives from the outside.
Never strip more than a third of a plant at once.
Keep mint in its own pot forever — planted in a bed it takes over everything.
tips: Leggy, pale, stretching growth means not enough light, not lack of water.
Basil is an annual and will die after flowering. Pinch out flower buds to keep it going.
proof: You cook with herbs you cut yourself, from plants still thriving three months on.
